title: What does NFTokenCreateOffer do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of NFTokenCreateOffer and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, NFTokenCreateOffer creates an on-ledger offer to buy or sell a particular NFT. [1]

Offer flags distinguish buying from selling, and optional destination and expiration fields constrain acceptance. An offer records trading terms; it does not transfer the NFT immediately. Check the NFT identifier and payment asset together. A zero-price transfer offer is still an ownership operation with permission and acceptance requirements. [1]

The NFTokenCreateOffer reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using NFTokenCreateOffer, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
